label: thm:main
scope: two_pole_test_of_certificate takes only the physical pair and Certificate.boxBounds from Proposition 6.1. It proves strict negative slope and the eventually strict quotient inequality, including the admissible domain.
printed_statement: \begin{theorem}\label{thm:main} Let $S(z)=-a_1/(z-\pole_1)-a_2/(z-\pole_2)$ with $a_1,a_2>0$ and $\operatorname{Im}\pole_1,\operatorname{Im}\pole_2<0$. Then $\slope(S)<0$. Consequently there is $\varepsilon_0=\varepsilon_0(S)>0$ such that \[ \Kq\bigl(S^{1+\varepsilon}\bigr)<\frac{\pi^2}{12}\qquad\text{for }0<\varepsilon<\varepsilon_0 . \] \end{theorem}

label: def:pick
scope: PickSum n has positive length, positive masses and lower-half-plane poles. Equal pole locations are allowed. PickSum.mass_pos, holomorphy and strict upper image are proved.
printed_statement: \begin{definition}\label{def:pick} A \emph{Pick sum} is a function \[ S(z)=-\sum_{j=1}^{n}\frac{a_j}{z-\pole_j},\qquad a_j>0,\quad \operatorname{Im}\pole_j<0 . \] Its \emph{total mass} is $\mass=a_1+\dots+a_n$. For $n=2$ we call $S$ a \emph{two-pole Pick function}. \end{definition}

label: lem:dirichlet
scope: dirichlet_annular_gradient quantifies an absolute constant before all smooth zero-boundary potentials, uses both actual suprema on the open upper half-annulus and includes boundary observations. dirichlet_cubic_decay bounds the potential and full real gradient for every r>1 with one constant depending only on the forcing bound.
printed_statement: \begin{lemma}[Dirichlet estimates]\label{lem:dirichlet} Let $V$ be smooth on $\overline{\U}$ and zero on $\R$, and write $r=|z|$. \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}] \item $|\nabla V(z)|\le C_0\bigl(r^{-1}\sup|V|+r\sup|\Delta V|\bigr)$, with the suprema over $\U\cap\{r/4<|z'|<2r\}$ and an absolute constant $C_0$. \item If $V$ is bounded and $|\Delta V|\le C(1+|z|)^{-3}$, then, as $r\to\infty$, $V=O((1+\log r)/r)$ and $\nabla V=O((1+\log r)/r^2)$, with constants that depend only on $C$. \end{enumerate} \end{lemma}

label: lem:far
scope: PickSum.far_field proves the true potential, full real Fréchet gradient and field asymptotics uniformly on both real rays and the open half-plane.
printed_statement: \begin{lemma}[Far field]\label{lem:far} Let $S$ be a Pick sum of total mass $\mass$, write $z=re^{i\theta}$, and put $U_0=\tfrac{i\mass}{2}\,\theta(\pi-\theta)$. As $r\to\infty$, uniformly in $\theta\in[0,\pi]$, \[ U_S=U_0+O\Bigl(\frac{1+\log r}{r}\Bigr),\qquad \nabla(U_S-U_0)=O\Bigl(\frac{1+\log r}{r^2}\Bigr),\qquad v_S=-\mass\,\frac{\pi/2-\theta}{z}+O\Bigl(\frac{1+\log r}{r^2}\Bigr). \] \end{lemma}

label: def:deficit
scope: The half-disc integral, its radial limit and normalized margin are defined. Existence is a separate obligation.
printed_statement: \begin{definition}[Deficit and margin]\label{def:deficit} For a Pick sum $S$ of total mass $\mass$, the \emph{deficit} of $S$ is \begin{equation}\label{eq:deficit} \Def(S)=\lim_{R\to\infty}\int_{\U\cap\{|z|<R\}}\bigl(\kz|S|^2-|v_S|^2\bigr)\,dA, \end{equation} and its \emph{margin} is $\marg(S)=\Def(S)/\mass^2-\kz$. \end{definition}

label: lem:deficit
scope: PickSum.finite_part and PickSum.finite_part_laws give unconditional existence, remainder integral formula, horizontal translation, spatial rescaling, reflection, and quadratic mass homogeneity for every finite positive Pick sum.
printed_statement: \begin{lemma}\label{lem:deficit} The limit \eqref{eq:deficit} exists and is finite. The deficit is unchanged when $S(z)$ is replaced by $S(z-x_0)$ with $x_0\in\R$, by $\lambda^{-1}S(z/\lambda)$ with $\lambda>0$, or by $-\overline{S(-\bar z)}$; and $\Def(cS)=c^2\Def(S)$ for $c>0$. In particular the margin depends only on the mass fractions $a_j/\mass$ and on the pole positions up to real translation, dilation and the reflection $\pole\mapsto-\bar\pole$. \end{lemma}

label: prop:liu-K
comparator_targets: Liu.analyticVectors_closed Liu.bergman_projection_range Liu.projection_has_kernel Liu.liu_norm_comparison Liu.bergmanLpNorm_operator_bound_iff Liu.TrialWindow.trial_difference_limit Liu.liuNorm_power_limit
scope: liu_norm_comparison proves both the sequence implication and strict excess throughout a punctured neighborhood of 2 for the sharp Lp norm of the actual Bergman kernel. The compensated trial variation is minus the L² residual energy and the gamma coefficient is π²/12. The residual bound is used almost everywhere.
printed_statement:
egin{proposition}\label{prop:liu-K} Let $F\in A^2$ have no zeros in $\U$, put $L= igl|\log|F| igr|$, and assume that for some $\eta_0>0$ \[ \int_\U|F|^p(1+L)^5\,dA<\infty\ 	ext{ for }|p-2|\le\eta_0 . \] Put $G=(I-\Bp)(F\log|F|)$, and assume also that $|G|\le C\,|F|\,(1+L)$ on $\U$ for some $C>0$. If $
orm{\Bp}_{L^{p_n}	o L^{p_n}}\le\lambda_{p_n}$ for a sequence $p_n	o2$, $p_n
e2$, then $\Kq(F)\le\kz$. Equivalently: if $\Kq(F)>\kz$, then $
orm{\Bp}_{L^p	o L^p}>\lambda_p$ for every $p
e2$ close enough to $2$. \end{proposition}

label: lem:liu-K-family
scope: PickSum.admissible_critical proves all conditions, including the actual residual with one constant over the upper half-plane, for all finite nonempty Pick sums and all printed exponents.
printed_statement: \begin{lemma}\label{lem:liu-K-family} Let $S$ be a Pick sum and $0<\varepsilon<1$. Then $F=S^{1+\varepsilon}$ satisfies the hypotheses of Proposition~\ref{prop:liu-K}, for every $0<\eta_0<2\varepsilon/(1+\varepsilon)$. \end{lemma}

label: prop:slope
scope: PickSum.slope_formula for every finite nonempty positive Pick sum. The actual quotient has slope 2(k0−Def(S)/m²), equal to minus twice the margin. PickSum.slope_remainder and PickSum.quotient_side_of_margin prove little-o and both strict sign conclusions.
printed_statement: \begin{proposition}[Slope formula]\label{prop:slope} Let $S$ be a Pick sum of total mass $\mass$. Then, as $\varepsilon\to0^+$, \[ \Kq\bigl(S^{1+\varepsilon}\bigr)=\kz+\slope(S)\,\varepsilon+o(\varepsilon),\qquad \slope(S)=2\Bigl(\kz-\frac{\Def(S)}{\mass^2}\Bigr)=-2\,\marg(S). \] \end{proposition}

label: cor:one-pole
scope: Deficit for every one-pole mass a>0 and every strictly lower pole is a²(3ζ(3)/4). The normalized margin and all printed decimals are verified.
printed_statement: \begin{corollary}[One pole]\label{cor:one-pole} For $S(z)=-a/(z-\pole)$ with $a>0$ and $\operatorname{Im}\pole<0$, \[ \Def(S)=\done\,a^2,\qquad \done=\tfrac34\zeta(3)=0.9015426\ldots,\qquad \marg(S)=\done-\kz=0.0790756\ldots>0 . \] \end{corollary}

label: thm:deficit
scope: pair_deficit_of_certificate takes only the physical pair and the fixed 168-box Certificate.boxBounds. The analytic proof supplies 5.1, 5.4 and E.4 and covers coincident poles.
printed_statement: \begin{theorem}\label{thm:deficit} Every two-pole Pick function $S$ of total mass $\mass$ satisfies $\Def(S)>\kz\,\mass^2$, that is, $\marg(S)>0$. \end{theorem}

label: def:witness
scope: isWitness encodes holomorphy, closure continuity and the uniform logarithmic far rate. truncatedWitness uses the specified centered half-disc.
printed_statement: \begin{definition}\label{def:witness} A \emph{witness} is a function $W$ that is analytic on $\U$, continuous on $\overline{\U}$, and satisfies $W(z)=\pi/2+O\bigl((1+\log r)/r\bigr)$ as $r\to\infty$, uniformly in $\theta$. For a Pick sum $S$ and a witness $W$ put \[ L_S[W]=\lim_{R\to\infty}\int_{D_R}\bigl(\kz|S|^2-|S|^2\,|\Arg S-W|^2\bigr)\,dA . \] \end{definition}

label: lem:orth
scope: PickSum.field_orthogonality has absolute integrability and zero pairing for the full printed test domain.
printed_statement: \begin{lemma}[Orthogonality]\label{lem:orth} Let $S$ be a Pick sum, and let $g$ be analytic on $\U$ and continuous on $\overline{\U}$, with $g=O\bigl((1+\log r)/r^2\bigr)$ as $r\to\infty$, uniformly in $\theta$. Then $v_S\bar g$ is integrable on $\U$ and \[ \int_\U v_S\,\bar g\,dA=0 . \] \end{lemma}

label: lem:witness
scope: PickSum.witness_identity includes the actual optimal witness, every printed witness, cutoff limit, inequality, and equality iff throughout the closed upper half-plane.
printed_statement: \begin{lemma}[Witness identity]\label{lem:witness} Let $S$ be a Pick sum and put $W^*_S=(f_S-v_S)/S$. Then $W^*_S$ is a witness, and for every witness $W$ the limit $L_S[W]$ exists and \[ L_S[W]=\Def(S)-\norm{S\,(W-W^*_S)}^2 . \] In particular $\Def(S)\ge L_S[W]$, with equality if and only if $W=W^*_S$. \end{lemma}

label: lem:cluster
scope: All positive masses and lower poles at d≤u/4, including equality and coincidence. Pair.mergedPole_lower proves the stronger loss 15 a₁a₂ d²/u² and Pair.mergedPole_deficit the printed 16.2 loss.
printed_statement: \begin{lemma}[Merged poles]\label{lem:cluster} Let $S$ be a two-pole Pick function with masses $a_1,a_2$, total mass $\mass$, mass fractions $\mu_j=a_j/\mass$, mass centre $\pole_c=\mu_1\pole_1+\mu_2\pole_2$ of depth $u_c=-\operatorname{Im}\pole_c>0$ and separation $d=|\pole_1-\pole_2|$. If $d\le u_c/4$, then \[ \Def(S)\ \ge\ \done\,\mass^2-16.2\,\mu_1\mu_2\,\mass^2\,\frac{d^2}{u_c(u_c-d)} . \] \end{lemma}

label: lem:smallmass
scope: Pair.small_mass_margin gives the strict 0.038 times the larger mass squared excess and positive normalized margin, for either ordering, all pole positions and mass ratio at most 1/4096. The blended finite-part lower bound uses the actual fields and witnesses.
printed_statement: \begin{lemma}[Small mass ratio]\label{lem:smallmass} Let $S$ be a two-pole Pick function, and let $m_1\ge m_2$ be its two masses (the masses $a_1,a_2$ in decreasing order), so that $\mass=m_1+m_2$. If $m_2\le2^{-12}m_1$, then for every position of the two poles \[ \Def(S)-\kz\,\mass^2\ >\ 0.038\,m_1^2 ; \] in particular $\marg(S)>0$. \end{lemma}

label: lem:flux
scope: depth_flux_hasDerivAt, depth_flux_contDiff and depth_flux_identity give the physical two-sided derivative, C¹ regularity and the signed finite-depth integral identity at all positive depths and both angular endpoints.
printed_statement: \begin{lemma}[Depth flux]\label{lem:flux} For fixed $(s,\gamma)$ the function $u\mapsto\marg(s,\gamma,u)$ is continuously differentiable on $(0,\infty)$, and \[ \frac{\partial\marg}{\partial u}(s,\gamma,u)=\flux(s,\gamma,u):=\int_{\R}\Bigl(|v_{S}(x)|^2-\kz\,|S(x)|^2\Bigr)\frac{dx}{\pi}, \qquad S=S_{s,\gamma,u}. \] Consequently $\marg(s,\gamma,u')=\marg(s,\gamma,u'')-\int_{u'}^{u''}\flux(s,\gamma,u)\,du$ for $0<u'<u''$. \end{lemma}

label: rem:onepole
scope: For any finite nonempty Pick sum, flux_law_at and finite_depth_flux_law apply to all real depth shifts that leave the poles strictly below the line. The physical derivative is continuous. The unconditional single-pole zero-flux identity includes every positive mass and depth and every real foot.
printed_statement: \begin{remark}\label{rem:onepole} The proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:flux} applies unchanged to every Pick sum. For a single pole the deficit does not depend on the depth (Lemma~\ref{lem:deficit}), so its flux is $0$: $\int_\R\bigl(|v_S|^2-\kz|S|^2\bigr)\,dx=0$. \end{remark}

label: lem:anchor
scope: depth_anchor proves the printed lower bound from the stated convergence of the improper flux integral. The finite-depth flux law and deep-cluster estimate are proved.
printed_statement: \begin{lemma}[Anchor]\label{lem:anchor} Fix $(s,\gamma)$ with $\gamma\in[0,\pi/2]$, and let $u>0$. If $\int_u^\infty\flux(s,\gamma,u')\,du'$ converges, then $\marg(s,\gamma,u)\ge(\done-\kz)-\int_u^\infty\flux(s,\gamma,u')\,du'$. \end{lemma}

label: lem:prefix
scope: The pointwise bound and its beta integral hold for all allowed parameters and depths exactly as printed. The proof uses E.3 and the Poisson-tested isolated moments.
printed_statement: \begin{lemma}[Small depth]\label{lem:prefix} For every $s\in\R$, every $\gamma\in[0,\pi/2]$ and $0<u\le1/4$, \[ |\flux(s,\gamma,u)|\le2^{34}\mu^{-2}\bigl(1+\log(1/u)\bigr),\qquad \mu=\min(a,b). \] Hence for $0<u\le u_0\le1/4$, $\int_u^{u_0}|\flux|\,du'\le\beta(u_0):=2^{34}\mu^{-2}u_0\bigl(2+\log(1/u_0)\bigr)$. \end{lemma}

label: lem:uniq
scope: halfPlane_probe_uniqueness uses the printed half-plane probes and closure/far-growth conditions. The central kernel pairing is absolutely integrable, all Cayley moments vanish, and the Bergman evaluation against every observing kernel is zero.
printed_statement: \begin{lemma}\label{lem:uniq} For $m\ge0$ let $g_m(z)=(z-i)^m(z+i)^{-m-3}$. Let $V$ be analytic on $\U$ and continuous on $\overline{\U}$, with $V(z)=O\bigl((1+\log|z|)/|z|\bigr)$ as $|z|\to\infty$. If $\int_{\U}V\,\bar g_m\,dA=0$ for every $m\ge0$, then $V=0$. \end{lemma}

label: lem:cap
scope: Actual cap quotient for every real 1<α<2, with explicit trigamma and gamma series, quadratic endpoint remainder and certified seven-decimal slope. The normalized Cayley monomials are complete for the physical projection and both differentiated Gauss sums have a summable majorant.
printed_statement: \begin{lemma}\label{lem:cap} For $1<\alpha<2$ let $F_\alpha(z)=(z+i)^{-\alpha}=\exp\bigl(-\alpha\operatorname{Log}(z+i)\bigr)$ on $\U$. Then \begin{equation}\label{eq:cap-exact} \Kq(F_\alpha)=\frac{\alpha^2}{4}\Bigl[2\psi_1(\alpha)-\frac{\Sigma_\alpha}{N_\alpha}\Bigr],\qquad N_\alpha=\frac{\Gamma(2\alpha-2)}{\Gamma(\alpha)^2},\qquad \Sigma_\alpha=\sum_{n\ge0}\Bigl(\frac{(2-\alpha)_n}{n!}\Bigr)^2\frac{\psi_1(n+2)}{n+1}. \end{equation} As $\varepsilon\to0^+$, \[ \Kq\bigl((z+i)^{-1-\varepsilon}\bigr)=\kz+\Bigl(\frac{\pi^2}{6}-\frac32\zeta(3)\Bigr)\varepsilon+O(\varepsilon^2), \qquad \frac{\pi^2}{6}-\frac32\zeta(3)=-0.1581512\ldots<0 . \] \end{lemma}

label: lem:one-pole-witness
scope: All four parts verified for the actual optimal witness at each positive mass and depth, any real foot, and every point of the closed upper half-plane. The correction attains its exact supremum log 2 at zero.
printed_statement: \begin{lemma}\label{lem:one-pole-witness} Let $S(z)=-a/(z-\pole_0)$ with $a>0$ and $\pole_0=x_0-iy_0$, $y_0>0$. Let $\omega$ be as in \eqref{eq:omega} and $q=\omega-\pi/2$. \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}] \item $q$ is analytic on $\U$, continuous on $\overline{\U}$, and $\sup_{\overline{\U}}|q|=\log2$. In particular, $\omega$ is a witness. \item $W^*_S(z)=\omega\bigl((z-x_0)/y_0\bigr)$. \item On $\overline{\U}$, $\bigl|\Arg S-W^*_S\bigr|\le\pi/2+\log2<2.264$. In particular, $|\operatorname{Re}(\Arg S-W^*_S)|<2.264$. \item On $\overline{\U}$, $\bigl|\kz-|\Arg S-W^*_S|^2\bigr|<4.304$. \end{enumerate} \end{lemma}

label: lem:C-proj
scope: SupercriticalSource.field_and_weak_projection proves continuity on the closed upper half-plane, the stated decay, square integrability and the actual projection identity for every weak L² primitive. weak_holomorphic_mem_analytic constructs a holomorphic representative without assuming differentiability of the primitive.
printed_statement: \begin{lemma}\label{lem:C-proj} Let $\rho$ be a smooth source on $\overline{\U}$ with $|\rho|\le C(1+|z|)^{-2-\varepsilon}$ for some $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$. Then $\mathcal C\rho$ is continuous on $\overline{\U}$ and $O(|z|^{-1-\varepsilon})$, so $\mathcal C\rho\in L^2$, and $\mathcal C\rho=(I-\Bp)h$ for every $h\in L^2$ with $\bar\partial h=\rho$. \end{lemma}

label: lem:sm-lambda
scope: smallMassFirstOrder_formula proves the signed identity via the convergent physical mixed cutoff and absolutely integrable complex correction. The real part of its integral has magnitude at most 79 for all second-pole positions.
printed_statement: \begin{lemma}\label{lem:sm-lambda} $\Psi_1=2\done+2\operatorname{Re}\mathcal Y$, where $\mathcal Y=\int_\U S_{\pole_1}\,\overline{(S_{\pole_2}-S_{\pole_1})}\,Q\,dA$ (absolutely convergent) and $Q=\kz-|\iota|^2-i\operatorname{Re}\iota$. Moreover $|\Psi_1-2\done|\le167$ for every position of $\pole_2$. \end{lemma}

label: lem:sm-remainder
scope: The actual three-term signed remainder for any two strictly lower poles and all 0<m≤1/10 exceeds or equals −m²(520+111 log(2/m)). Its three integrals converge absolutely.
printed_statement: \begin{lemma}\label{lem:sm-remainder} For $m_2\le1/10$ and every position of $\pole_2$, $\Psi_2\ge-m_2^2(520+111L_{m_2})$. \end{lemma}

label: lem:ratlog
scope: PickSum.rational_log_formula gives the actual physical field throughout the closed upper half-plane, including all numerator zeros with multiplicity and the derivative value at each removable log quotient. It identifies the true zero multiset for distinct lower poles.
printed_statement: \begin{lemma}\label{lem:ratlog} For every Pick sum $S$ as above and every $z\in\overline{\U}$, \[ v_S(z)=\frac i2\sum_{j=1}^n\sum_{k=1}^{2n-1}(-a_j)\,\nu_k\,\mathcal T_{\pole_j,c_k}(z). \] \end{lemma}

label: lem:analytic-window
scope: admissible_contour_independence gives an admissible path, absolute integrability and independence for every locally absolutely continuous admissible contour. mass_window_continuation rules out all nine collisions on the open mass strip, produces the global analytic extension and identifies all real physical fluxes.
printed_statement: \begin{lemma}\label{lem:analytic-window} Let $\gamma\in[0,\pi/2]$ and $u>0$ be real. In $H$, use for $\operatorname{Log}(z-c)$ the branch whose cut runs vertically down from each node $c$ and up from each partner: $\arg(z-c)\in(-\pi/2,3\pi/2)$ for a node $c$ and $\arg(z-c^\#)\in(-3\pi/2,\pi/2)$ for a partner $c^\#$; at real parameters these agree with the principal value on $\R$. For each constant logarithm use the branch continued from its half-plane at real parameters, with its cut on the half of the imaginary axis outside that half-plane: $i[0,\infty)$ for an argument $c-c'^\#$, which lies in the lower half-plane at real parameters, and $-i[0,\infty)$ for $c'^\#-c$. Call a path \emph{admissible} if it equals $\R$ outside a bounded set and meets none of these cuts. \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}] \item An admissible path exists, and the integral of $H$ is the same along all of them, as long as no node lies directly above a partner (same real part, imaginary part at least as large). \item For $|\operatorname{Im}s|<\pi/2$ no node lies directly above a partner. \item Hence $s\mapsto\frac1\pi\int H$, along any admissible path, is analytic on the strip $|\operatorname{Im}s|<\pi/2$, and equals $\flux$ at real $s$. \end{enumerate} \end{lemma}

label: prop:certificate
scope: The sole explicit numerical hypothesis states (a) and (b) for the 168 fixed threshold and lower-bound pairs in boxes.tsv. certified_prefix_integral proves the analytic prefix bound for every box independently of that hypothesis. Lean also checks the cover and beta arithmetic.
printed_statement: \begin{proposition}\label{prop:certificate} For each box $B$ of the cover of Section~\ref{sec:covers} there are numbers $0<u_B\le1/4$ and $\bB>\beta_B\ge0$, with $\beta_B$ as above, such that for every $(s,\gamma)\in B$: \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}] \item $\marg(s,\gamma,u)>0$ for every $u\ge u_B$; \item $\marg(s,\gamma,u_B)\ge \bB$. \end{enumerate} \end{proposition}

label: lem:top
scope: top_reciprocal_lemma proves reciprocal scaling, holomorphic extension on the open unit disc and bounded scaled flux on the top ray, for the full closed angular range [0,π].
printed_statement: \begin{lemma}\label{lem:top} Let $s$ and $\gamma$ be real, $0\le\gamma\le\pi$. For $\tilde u\ge0$ let $\flux_{\tilde u}$ be the boundary integral of Lemma~\ref{lem:flux} for the function $-a/(z+i)-b/(z+i-\tilde ue^{-i\gamma})$, with $a,b$ as in \eqref{eq:normal}, and let $\flux(s,\gamma,u)$ be that integral for the function \eqref{eq:normal} also when $\gamma>\pi/2$. Then $u^2\flux(s,\gamma,u)=\tilde u^{-1}\flux_{\tilde u}$ for $u>0$ and $\tilde u=1/u$, and $\tilde u\mapsto\tilde u^{-1}\flux_{\tilde u}$ extends analytically to the disc $|\tilde u|<1$. In particular $u^2\flux(s,\gamma,u)$ is bounded for $u\ge e^{1/2}$. \end{lemma}

label: lem:chain
scope: depth_chain_from_tests and box_conclusions_from_chain_tests give both box conclusions from the printed strict signed suffix tests and weak endpoint test. Absolute convergence of every positive physical top tail is proved.
printed_statement: \begin{lemma}\label{lem:chain} Suppose that for every $(s,\gamma)\in B$ \begin{equation}\label{eq:chain} I_k(u)+\sum_{j>k}I_j(u_j)<\done-\kz\quad\text{for every $k$ and every $u\in[u_k,u_{k+1}]$,}\qquad \done-\kz-\sum_{j\ge0}I_j(u_j)\ge \bB . \end{equation} Then \textup{(a)} and \textup{(b)} of Proposition~\ref{prop:certificate} hold on $B$. \end{lemma}

label: lem:cheb
scope: firstKind_ellipse_error proves the printed uniform bound on the closed interval for all degrees including zero, with the actual first-kind Lagrange polynomial and focal-distance ellipse. It uses no H4.
printed_statement: \begin{lemma}\label{lem:cheb} Let $\chi$ be analytic on a neighbourhood of $E_\upsilon$ with $|\chi|\le M$ there, and let $\chi_n$ be its polynomial interpolant of degree $n$ at the $n+1$ points of the first kind. Then $\max_{[-1,1]}|\chi-\chi_n|\le4M\upsilon^{-n}/(\upsilon-1)$. \end{lemma}

label: lem:tensor
scope: The full 6.5 claim uses the refereed external result H4 (Ibrahimoglu, §3.2, equation (13), DOI 10.1186/s13660-016-1030-3) as an explicit argument. The pointwise cardinal-sum tensor estimate on the three printed mixed domains and the complex-to-real cardinal identity are proved independently.
printed_statement: \begin{lemma}\label{lem:tensor} Let $\mathcal{L}_n=1+\frac2\pi\log(n+1)$. For every $n\ge1$, $\mathcal{L}_n$ is an upper bound for the Lebesgue constant of interpolation at the $n+1$ points of the first kind (classical; see~\cite[(13)]{Ibrahimoglu}, where $n$ is also the degree). Let $\Pi_1$, $\Pi_2$, $\Pi_3$ denote interpolation in $\xi_1$, $\xi_2$, $\xi_3$. Let $M_3\ge|\flux_\xi|$ on ($\xi_3\in E_{\upsilon_3}$)$\times$($\xi_1,\xi_2\in[-1,1]$), let $M_2\ge|\flux_\xi|$ on ($\xi_2\in E_{\upsilon_2}$)$\times$($\xi_1\in[-1,1]$)$\times$($\xi_3$ at the interpolation points), and let $M_1\ge|\flux_\xi|$ on ($\xi_1\in E_{\upsilon_1}$)$\times$($\xi_2\in[-1,1]$)$\times$($\xi_3$ at the interpolation points), $\flux_\xi$ being analytic in the complex variable on each of these sets. Then on $[-1,1]^3$ \[ |\flux_\xi-\hat \flux_\xi|\le \mathrm{Err}:=\mathrm{Err}_3+\mathcal{L}_{n_3}\mathrm{Err}_2+\mathcal{L}_{n_3}\mathcal{L}_{n_2}\mathrm{Err}_1,\qquad \mathrm{Err}_m=4M_m\upsilon_m^{-n_m}/(\upsilon_m-1). \] \end{lemma}

label: lem:analytic
scope: interpolation_cell_analytic gives the ordinary and reciprocal-depth physical flux extensions on the closed ellipse under the stated node and partner signs, for affine and logarithmic coordinates. top_focus_limit proves that the true real limiting value at the coalescent focus is zero.
printed_statement: \begin{lemma}\label{lem:analytic} For real values of the other two variables, $\flux_\xi$ extends analytically in each variable to the region used for it in Lemma~\ref{lem:tensor}, provided that on that region the nodes of $S$ stay in the lower half-plane and their partners stay in the upper half-plane (proof in Appendix~\ref{app:flux}). At the top cell this holds in the variable $\tilde u$ also through $\tilde u=0$, where the nodes merge (Lemma~\ref{lem:top}). \end{lemma}

label: lem:tail
scope: subtracted_flux_tail_bound and moved_flux_tail_bound give the printed coefficient and both real tails for complex masses and independent partners, including equality at the cutoff. Pair.tail_subtraction_agrees verifies the actual physical integrand.
printed_statement: \begin{lemma}\label{lem:tail} Suppose that $x_{\max}\ge10^{18}$ and $x_{\max}>4|c|$ for every node and partner $c$. Then, on $\R$ and on the moved path below, for $|x|\ge x_{\max}$ \[ |H_\times(x)|\le\bigl(c_\times\Upsilon(x)^2+8\kz|a_1a_2|\bigr)x^{-2},\qquad c_\times=8|a_1a_2|+32\bigl(|a_1|+|a_2|\bigr)^2 . \] \end{lemma}

label: lem:taylor
scope: centred_taylor_flux proves the exact constant Taylor coefficient, absolute integrability and vanishing integrals of both coefficients, and the flux remainder identity for arbitrary complex masses and independent partners satisfying separation throughout the motion. The normalized physical flux is identified.
printed_statement: \begin{lemma}\label{lem:taylor} Suppose that for every $t\in[0,1]$ the moved nodes lie below $\R$ and their partners above it. Then $H_\times(x;t)$ is analytic in $t$ on a neighbourhood of $[0,1]$; its Taylor coefficients $H^{[k]}$ at $t=0$ satisfy $H^{[0]}=2a_1a_2h_{\pole_c}$ and $\int_\R H^{[0]}\,dx=\int_\R H^{[1]}\,dx=0$, at real and at complex parameters; and $\pi\flux=\int_\R(H_\times-H^{[0]}-H^{[1]})\,dx$, where $H_\times=H_\times(\cdot\,;1)$. \end{lemma}

scope: Full boundary decomposition, absolute integrability, integrated flux identity, explicit cross pairing, isolated traces and both bounds verified over the physical domain. The reciprocal distance bound is used off the foot.
printed_statement: \begin{lemma}\label{lem:trace} For $u>0$ let $\mathcal V_j=T_u\hat\rho_j$, $c_u=T_u\operatorname{Re}\hat\rho_\times$ and $q_u=T_u\operatorname{Im}\hat\rho_\times$. Then $|v_S|=|\mathcal V_1+\mathcal V_2+c_u+iq_u|$ on $\R$ for $S=S_{s,\gamma,u}$, and \begin{equation}\label{eq:fluxdec} \flux(s,\gamma,u)=\int_\R\bigl(2\mathcal V_1\mathcal V_2+2(\mathcal V_1+\mathcal V_2)c_u+c_u^2+q_u^2\bigr)\frac{dx}\pi -2\kz\operatorname{Re}\langle aS_{\pole_1},bS_{\pole_2}\rangle_\R, \end{equation} where $S_\pole=-1/(z-\pole)$ (Section~\ref{sec:enclose}) and $2\operatorname{Re}\langle aS_{\pole_1},bS_{\pole_2}\rangle_\R=4ab\,(\sin\gamma+2u)/\bigl(\cos^2\gamma+(\sin\gamma+2u)^2\bigr)$. For the single pole $a_jS_{\pole_j}$ alone the cross terms vanish, so $\mathcal V_j=|v_{a_jS_{\pole_j}}|$ on $\R$; with its foot $x_1=0$, $x_2=\cos\gamma$ and its depth $y_1=u$, $y_2=\sin\gamma+u$, \begin{equation}\label{eq:iso} \mathcal V_j(x)=a_j\int_{y_j}^\infty\frac{t\,dt}{(t+y_j)\bigl((x-x_j)^2+t^2\bigr)},\qquad 0\le\mathcal V_j(x)\le\min\Bigl(\frac{a_j}{y_j},\frac{\pi a_j}{2|x-x_j|}\Bigr), \end{equation} where $a_1=a$, $a_2=b$. \end{lemma}

label: lem:MR
scope: Full physical rational formula, actual derivative, nonpositive real part, modulus and all three distance bounds.
printed_statement: \begin{lemma}\label{lem:MR} Let $r_1=|Z|$, $r_2=|Z-e^{-i\gamma}|$, $r_*=|Z-ae^{-i\gamma}|$ and $Y_\gamma=X\sin\gamma+Y\cos\gamma$. Then \[ \hat\rho_\times=\frac{2iab\,e^{i\gamma}Y_\gamma}{r_1^2r_2^2(\bar Z-ae^{i\gamma})},\qquad \operatorname{Re}\hat\rho_\times=-\frac{2ab\,Y_\gamma^2}{r_1^2r_2^2r_*^2}\le0,\qquad |\hat\rho_\times|=\frac{2ab\,|Y_\gamma|}{r_1^2r_2^2r_*}, \] and $|Y_\gamma|\le\min(r_1,r_2,r_*)$. \end{lemma}

label: lem:mixededge
scope: mixed_edge_flux_estimate gives a single coefficient 2a times the physical regular trace at zero depth and the shallow foot. Its magnitude is bounded by 64/sin⁴γ and the uniform residual by 4096/(a² sin⁸γ) for every 0<u≤1/4 and every physical angle with positive sine.
printed_statement: \begin{lemma}\label{lem:mixededge} Let $\sin\gamma>0$. There is a real number $c_{\log}=c_{\log}(s,\gamma)$ with $|c_{\log}|\le64/\sin^4\gamma$ such that for $0<u\le\frac14$ \[ \bigl|\flux(s,\gamma,u)-c_{\log}\log(1/u)\bigr|\le\frac{4096}{a^2\sin^8\gamma}. \] \end{lemma}
